paragraphs.text: Or, “you elders.” Heb., haz·zeqe·nimʹ; Gr., pre·sbyʹte·roi. See Ac 15:2 ftn.
“The creeping, unwinged locust.” Heb., hai·yaʹleq. See Ps 105:34 ftn.
“Owner.” Heb., baʹʽal; Gr., anʹdra; Lat., viʹrum, “husband.”
Or, “Feel shame, you farmers; howl, you vinedressers.”
“From the Almighty One.” Heb., mi·Shad·daiʹ. Compare Ge 17:1 ftn.

“Like the garden of Eden.” Heb., keghan-ʽEʹdhen; Gr., hos pa·raʹdei·sos try·phesʹ, “Like a paradise of delight”; Syr., ʼaikh par·dai·saʼ daʽ·den; Lat., quaʹsi horʹtus vo·lu·ptaʹtis, “Like a garden of pleasure.”
Or, “Hold sacred; Treat as holy.” Heb., qad·deshuʹ; Gr., ha·gi·aʹsa·te; Lat., sanc·ti·fi·caʹte.
Lit., “hinder,” that is, to one’s back when facing east.
MLXX end chap. 2 here; TLXXBagsterSyVg continue chap. 2 through vs 32 (3:5 of M).
“My spirit.” Heb., ru·chiʹ; Gr., pneuʹma·tos; Lat., spiʹri·tum.
“In among the survivors,” MVg; Gr., eu·ag·ge·li·zoʹme·noi, “those telling good news; those evangelizing.”
MLXX end chap. 3 here; TLXXBagsterSyVg end chap. 2.
Lit., “for the prostitute.” Heb., baz·zoh·nahʹ; Gr., porʹnais; Lat., in pro·stiʹbu·lum.
Lit., “what are you to me?” A Heb. idiom; a repellent question indicating objection to the “treatment.” See App 7B.
“Men of.” Heb., ʼan·shehʹ, pl. of ʼish.
“And I will avenge their blood and by no means consider [them] innocent,” LXX; Vg, “And I will cleanse their blood that I had not cleansed.”
